title: Hány órát dolgozol?: Duration with the Accusative

sections.title: Marking how long, not what
sections.content: You already know the accusative -t for direct objects, and you've seen it used for duration too, as in nyolc órát alszom ("I sleep eight hours"). The same pattern answers Hány órát dolgozol? ("How many hours do you work?") — put -t on the number of hours, even though nothing is technically being "acted on": Nyolc órát dolgozom naponta.

items.english: How many hours do you work per day?

items.spanish: Nyolc órát dolgozom, és délben egy órát tartok szünetet.
items.english: I work eight hours, and at noon I take a one-hour break.

items.spanish: Ma sok a túlóra, nagyon fárasztó ez a hét.
items.english: There's a lot of overtime today, this week is very tiring.

sections.content: tart szünetet ("takes a break") puts the accusative on szünet the same way — egy órát tartok szünetet literally strings two accusatives together, "[for] an hour I hold [a] break," which feels odd word for word but is completely natural in Hungarian.
